note.explanation: Plant and animal cells have structures suited to their jobs. Plant cell walls support and protect cells, chloroplasts make food, and large vacuoles help keep cells firm. Animal cells have structures such as centrioles and lysosomes, and their lack of a rigid cell wall lets them change shape.
examples: A plant cell wall supports and protects the cell.
A sperm cell uses its flagellum to move toward the egg.
note.checkAnswer: The large central vacuole stores water, nutrients, and waste products. It provides turgor pressure that maintains cell shape.
note.simple: Cell structures are parts with particular jobs. Plant cells have structures that help them stay supported and make food. Animal cells have structures that help with cell division, cleanup, and movement.

mcqs.stem: What material makes the rigid plant cell wall described in this section?
rationales: Correct: the section states that plant cell walls are made of cellulose.
Incorrect: protein is not named as the material of the plant cell wall in this section.
Incorrect: starch is not named as the material of the plant cell wall in this section.

mcqs.stem: What is the main advantage of chloroplasts in plant cells?
rationales: Incorrect: making spindle fibres is the role of centrioles in animal cells.
Incorrect: storing water and nutrients is a role of the large central vacuole.
Correct: chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, helping plants produce food.
Incorrect: breaking down waste materials is a role of lysosomes.

options: It allows direct communication between cells.
mcqs.stem: How does the large central vacuole help maintain a plant cell's shape?
rationales: Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres during cell division.
Correct: the large central vacuole provides turgor pressure that maintains cell shape.
Incorrect: plasmodesmata allow direct communication and transport between plant cells.
Incorrect: lysosomes break down waste materials.

mcqs.stem: Which plant cell structures allow direct communication and transport of substances between cells?
rationales: Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres during cell division.
Correct: plasmodesmata are channels for communication and transport between plant cells.
Incorrect: chloroplasts convert light energy into chemical energy.
Incorrect: flagella are involved in movement, such as the movement of sperm cells.

options: They ensure accurate distribution of chromosomes during cell division.
They let plant cells produce food.
mcqs.stem: What is the advantage of centrioles in animal cells?
rationales: Correct: centrioles make spindle fibres, ensuring accurate chromosome distribution during cell division.
Incorrect: turgor pressure is provided by the large central vacuole in plant cells.
Incorrect: lysosomes, rather than centrioles, break down waste materials.
Incorrect: chloroplasts allow plants to produce food through photosynthesis.

mcqs.stem: Which animal cell structures contain enzymes that break down waste materials?
rationales: Correct: lysosomes contain enzymes that break down waste materials and contribute to cellular cleanup and recycling.
Incorrect: chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.
Incorrect: plasmodesmata connect plant cells for communication and transport.
Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres for cell division.

options: They make chemical energy from light.
mcqs.stem: What advantage do animal cells gain from lacking a rigid cell wall?
rationales: Correct: without a rigid cell wall, animal cells can change shape easily, helping with movements.
Incorrect: converting light energy into chemical energy is the role of chloroplasts.
Incorrect: turgor pressure is provided by the large central vacuole in plant cells.
Incorrect: centrioles make spindle fibres, not the lack of a cell wall.

mcqs.stem: Which structure propels a sperm cell toward the egg?
rationales: Correct: the section gives the sperm cell's flagellum as the structure that propels it toward the egg.
Incorrect: the large central vacuole stores materials and provides turgor pressure in plant cells.
Incorrect: plasmodesmata connect plant cells for communication and transport.
Incorrect: a rigid cell wall supports and protects plant cells; it does not propel sperm.

written.text: Write any four differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
written.finalAnswer: Plant cells have a rigid cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts, a large central vacuole, and plasmodesmata. Animal cells lack a rigid cell wall, allowing them to change shape easily; they have centrioles and lysosomes, and some have cilia or flagella.

modelAnswer: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose; animal cells lack a rigid cell wall and can change shape easily.

examTips: A short question may ask for the function of one structure, such as a lysosome, vacuole, or centriole. Name the structure and state its function clearly.
A long question may ask you to compare plant and animal cells. Give distinct paired differences rather than listing features without saying which cell has them.
For questions about advantages, connect the structure to what it helps the cell do: for example, a rigid wall provides support and protection.
Use the textbook's exact terms, including cellulose, turgor pressure, plasmodesmata, and spindle fibres.

explain.title: Plant cell wall
explain.body: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose. It provides structural support and protection.

explain.title: Chloroplasts and vacuole
explain.body: They contain chloroplasts, which are responsible for photosynthesis. Chloroplasts convert light energy into chemical energy, allowing plants to produce food. The large central vacuole stores water, nutrients, and waste products. It provides turgor pressure that maintains cell shape.

explain.title: Connections between plant cells
explain.body: Plant cells are interconnected by plasmodesmata, channels that allow direct communication and transport of substances between cells.

explain.title: Animal-cell structures and flexibility
explain.body: Animal cells have centrioles which make spindle fibres. This ensures the accurate distribution of chromosomes during cell division. They contain lysosomes, filled with enzymes that break down waste materials. Lysosomes contribute to cellular cleanup and recycling. Some animal cells have structures called flagella and cilia, which are involved in movement. Animal cells lack a rigid cell wall, allowing them to change shape easily.

mistakes: Do not say that lysosomes make spindle fibres; the section assigns that job to centrioles.
Do not confuse the vacuole's storage role with the chloroplast's role in photosynthesis.
When explaining turgor pressure, say that it helps maintain cell shape.
Do not say that animal cells have a rigid cell wall; the section says they lack one.
Do not describe plasmodesmata as movement structures; they allow communication and transport between plant cells.
